newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico same-day peso tumbles, 48-hr rate soft.
newsitem.headline: Mexico same-day peso tumbles, 48-hr rate soft.

text.p: Mexico's same-day peso, which had not traded since Friday, plunged over 13 centavos at the close on Tuesday, with other contracts tenuously stable.
"The market seems to be settling down at new levels in trading by both locals and foreigners," a trader said, pointing out that the market was still nervous and volatile.
The same-day peso closed 13.2 centavos weaker at 7.7250/7.7350 per dollar.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart were meanwhile both 0.5 of a centavo weaker at 7.7380/7.7450 and 7.7320/7.7400 per dollar, respectively.
Traders said the peso had also been harmed by revised Mexican government privatization plans for the petrochemical industry, whereby the government would retain a majority stake.
"The petrochemical sell-off has not been handled well...foreigners may hold back investment as a way to bring pressure to bear to obtain a better plan," said a trader.
